Scope (unchanged): only the search near the offset a hybrid table's /Prev names (the chain-loop call site), and only where that table's /XRefStm read a cross-reference stream in the stream's place (readInStreamsPlace is { Kind: Stream }, read whole or in part, not lost). The deferral of 394028c applied under the same condition, but acted only on that stream. Within the scope it now acts on every stream candidate. It does not apply to the /XRefStm's own search, startxref, plain /Prev searches, or an /XRefStm that read a classic table.

Cost: nothing more is read to tell. The /XRefStm's stream is judged by the dictionary its reading kept (Trailer). Any other place's dictionary is the one its reading parses first. TryParseNumberedAt's keep predicate refuses a stream that may be the table's own, so its data is neither decoded nor read as rows, and nothing is reported or recorded except an endstream search. A place so passed over is parsed again (one window of up to 64 KB) only when the search comes back to it, and it counts again toward MaxRelocationCandidates (32). A deferred place never retried now costs less than before, since it is not decoded. The candidate list grows by at most the places in the window. Each read in scope allocates one closure, at most 32 per document plus retries.

deviations: Deferred streams are tried in a single nearest-first order. The /XRefStm's stream, when its /Prev names the table's offset, is no longer tried last after the others: it takes its place among them by distance. The decision says each 'is tried after every other place', which cannot hold for two such streams at once. The nearest-first-among-deferred test pins the order chosen.

A /Prev is compared as written. Only a direct integer equal to the table's /Prev offset counts as 'naming the offset the table's /Prev names'. A reference is not followed, to read nothing more. A real or other non-integer counts as another offset. /Prev null counts as none, because the parser leaves it out (7.3.7). The MayBeTablesOwn XML doc says so.

The deferral of other streams applies whenever the /XRefStm read a stream, even when that stream lies outside the search window. That is the same condition the 394028c deferral was guarded by. Before, nothing was reordered when the stream was not in the window.

Small refactor: the in-scope parse lives in a new private TryParseNearHybridPrev. This avoids duplicating the TryParseNumberedAt call and the guard line, and keeps the closure allocation to in-scope reads.

When a `/Prev` or an `/XRefStm` names an offset its section does not start at, short of it or past it, `PdfFileReader.TryRelocateXRefSection` tries each place near the offset, nearest first. `IsTokenOnItsLine` lexes the place's line alone, from its start, so it does not see stream data that an earlier line opened. In stream data whose bytes hold the text as written, it therefore takes:

- the word `xref`, wherever its line, lexed alone, reads it as a token, its middle included: `The xref tables …` as well as a line that starts with it;
- the header of an object whose dictionary gives `/Type /XRef`, such as an example the data quotes.

Stream data holds the text as written under no filter, as an embedded file that holds prose does, and also under a filter that keeps it byte for byte: a `/FlateDecode` stream written with a stored block (zlib level 0, which .NET's `CompressionLevel.NoCompression` writes), or the literal runs of `/RunLengthDecode`. Ordinary deflate output scatters the word, and the search then reads the file as main does.

No load lexes an embedded file's data. An object stream's members are lexed by a load, as an object's body is, and stay out of this case. But a place in such data declares itself a section and, being the nearest place, it ends the search. It cannot be read, so the reader:
